beats.title: Austria's Red-White-Red Legend
beats.description: At a crusader siege, a duke's blood-soaked white tunic was said to leave a white band across red, birthing a banner.
beats.note: Traditional legend (Siege of Acre); not documented in Austrian sources

beats.title: The Dannebrog Falls From the Sky
beats.description: During a crusade battle in Estonia, a red banner with a white cross was said to drop from heaven and rally the Danes.
beats.why_in: legendary first raising of Denmark's flag
beats.note: Traditional date of the Battle of Lyndanisse legend

beats.title: The First Union Flag
beats.description: England and Scotland's crosses were merged into one design for ships of both kingdoms under a single king.

beats.title: The Grand Union Flag Is Raised
beats.description: Rebel colonists flew a banner of thirteen red and white stripes with the old crosses in the corner aboard a warship.
beats.why_in: first American flag raised, the Continental Colours
beats.note: First recorded raising aboard USS Alfred, December 1775; traditional Prospect Hill raising is 1 January 1776 but disputed

beats.title: The Stars and Stripes Adopted
beats.description: Congress resolved that the new republic's flag would have thirteen alternating red and white stripes and thirteen stars.

beats.title: Spain Adopts Red and Yellow
beats.description: A king ordered a new naval ensign in red and yellow stripes so ships could be told apart from other nations' white flags.

beats.title: France Adopts the Tricolour
beats.description: The revolutionary assembly decreed that the national flag would carry three vertical bands of blue, white and red.

beats.title: Italy's Tricolore First Flown
beats.description: A green, white and red banner was adopted by a short-lived republic in northern Italy, the ancestor of the national flag.

beats.title: St Patrick's Cross Joins the Flag
beats.description: With the union of Great Britain and Ireland, a red diagonal cross was added to the flag, giving the design still used.

beats.title: Miranda Raises Venezuela's Flag
beats.description: A Venezuelan revolutionary hoisted a yellow, blue and red flag aboard his ship on an expedition to free his homeland.

beats.title: Belgrano Raises Argentina's Flag
beats.description: A general on the banks of the Paraná River unfurled a sky-blue and white banner for his troops, to the government's displeasure.

beats.title: Chile Adopts the Lone Star Flag
beats.description: Chile's leader chose a white, blue and red banner with a single white star, as the country fought off Spanish rule.

beats.title: Norway Adopts Its Nordic Cross
beats.description: A red flag with a blue-and-white cross was chosen for the kingdom, though it was long kept off the sea.

beats.title: Greece Adopts Blue and White
beats.description: The Greek national assembly chose a flag of nine stripes and a white cross, said to echo the syllables of a battle cry.

beats.title: Belgium Adopts Black-Yellow-Red
beats.description: The new kingdom confirmed a tricolour taken from the colours of the uprising against Dutch rule.
beats.note: Colours first flown in 1830; adopted 23 January 1831

beats.title: The Ottoman Star and Crescent
beats.description: A red flag bearing a white crescent and star was fixed as the empire's official design, the root of the Turkish flag.
beats.note: Five-pointed-star version adopted 1844; motif used on ships from 1793

beats.title: The Irish Tricolour Is Presented
beats.description: A nationalist leader returning from France showed a green, white and orange flag meant to join two traditions in peace.

beats.title: Cuba's Lone Star Flag Is Raised
beats.description: A filibustering expedition landed at Cárdenas and hoisted a banner of blue and white stripes with a red triangle and star.

beats.title: Japan Fixes the Rising Sun Flag
beats.description: A red disc on white was decreed as the design for merchant ships, soon the symbol of the nation.
beats.note: Proclamation No. 57 of 1870 (merchant ships); national flag by law in 1999

beats.title: Brazil Raises Green and Gold
beats.description: Days after the monarchy fell, a new banner with a yellow diamond and blue globe replaced the imperial flag.

beats.title: The Philippine Flag Is Unfurled
beats.description: From a window of a family mansion near Manila, a sun-and-stars banner sewn in exile was shown as independence was proclaimed.
beats.why_in: first official raising of the Philippine flag
beats.note: Raised at Kawit 12 June 1898; first battle use 28 May 1898

beats.title: The Australian Flag Is First Flown
beats.description: Following a nationwide design contest, the new federation's flag with the Southern Cross flew over Melbourne.

beats.title: Thailand Adopts Its Tricolour
beats.description: A king replaced an elephant flag with horizontal bands of red, white and blue, matching the colours of his wartime allies.

beats.title: Germany Adopts Black-Red-Gold
beats.description: The new republic chose a tricolour whose colours dated back to the liberal movements of the previous century.

beats.title: The Hammer and Sickle Flag
beats.description: The union of socialist republics fixed a red flag bearing a crossed hammer and sickle beneath a gold-bordered star.
beats.note: Hammer-and-sickle flag adopted 1923; a first flag was adopted in December 1922

beats.title: Nationalist China Adopts a Flag
beats.description: A red field with a white sun on a blue canton became the flag of the government in Nanjing, later used in Taiwan.

beats.title: India's Tricolour Adopted
beats.description: The constituent assembly approved a saffron, white and green flag, with a wheel of law at its centre, just before freedom.

beats.title: Israel Adopts the Star of David
beats.description: A provisional council chose a white flag with blue stripes and a blue hexagram, based on a prayer-shawl design.

beats.title: China's Five-Star Flag Is Raised
beats.description: Over a huge crowd in Beijing, a red flag with a large gold star and four smaller ones was hoisted for the first time.

beats.title: Ghana Raises Red, Gold, Green
beats.description: A black star on a tricolour flew over the first sub-Saharan colony to win freedom, setting a style many nations copied.

beats.title: Nepal's Double Pennant Flag
beats.description: A constitution fixed the design of two stacked crimson triangles, making the only national flag that is not a rectangle.

beats.title: Canada Raises the Maple Leaf
beats.description: A red and white flag with a single maple leaf replaced the Red Ensign on Parliament Hill after a long national debate.

beats.title: The UAE Flag Is Raised
beats.description: Seven sheikhdoms joined under a flag of pan-Arab red, green, white and black, hoisted by the ruler of Abu Dhabi.

beats.title: Bangladesh Adopts Its Flag
beats.description: After a war of separation, the new republic formally fixed a flag with a red circle on a deep green field.
beats.note: Official adoption 17 January 1972; earlier version with a map flown in 1971

beats.title: Zimbabwe Raises Its Flag
beats.description: A new flag with a white triangle, red star and the Zimbabwe Bird replaced the colonial banner at midnight celebrations.

beats.title: Russia's Tricolour Returns
beats.description: After a failed hardline coup, the white, blue and red tricolour replaced the hammer and sickle as the Russian republic's banner.
beats.note: Hoisted and adopted 22 August 1991 (de facto); de jure November 1991

beats.title: South Africa's New Flag
beats.description: A six-colour design with a sideways Y was raised just before the country's first all-race elections.

beats.title: Kosovo Unveils Its Flag
beats.description: A blue flag with a gold map of the country and six white stars was shown as a new Balkan state declared itself.

beats.title: South Sudan Raises Its Flag
beats.description: The world's newest country hoisted a black, red and green flag with a blue triangle and gold star at its birth ceremony.
